# Using the library

## Build a checkout

Install Lean's toolchain manager. The committed [`lean-toolchain`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/main/lean-toolchain)
selects Lean 4.34.1, and [`lake-manifest.json`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/main/lake-manifest.json) fixes the dependency
revisions:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments.git hypertournaments
cd hypertournaments
lake env true
lake exe cache get $(python3 tools/project_sources.py --mathlib-roots)
lake build
lake env lean docs/Examples.lean
```

The cache command downloads the precompiled Mathlib modules used by the
project. The project and its vendored Ramsey proof modules are checked by
the subsequent build.

## Import the results

The umbrella import exposes the documented results:

```lean
import Hypertournaments

open Hypertournaments

example {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (family : ForbiddenFamily n)
    (hpc : ∀ m F, F ∈ family m → PairCancelling F) :
    HasStrongAmalgamation family :=
  pair_cancelling_hasStrongAmalgamation hn family hpc
```

This example is compiled in [`docs/Examples.lean`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/main/docs/Examples.lean). Its conclusion is
ordinary finite strong amalgamation of the omission class, with arbitrary
orientation-preserving source injections and exact overlap of the two sides.
The forbidden family may be infinite.

For a smaller import, use the defining module listed in the relevant
[main-article](Main-article), [potential](Generalised-potential-structures)
or [classification](Classification) entry. For example:

```lean
import Hypertournaments.PositiveClassification

#check Hypertournaments.amalgamation_classification
```

The full `#check` command displays all implicit parameters and hypotheses in
your local Lean environment. The statement map also provides a direct link
to the source declaration.

## Use a pinned dependency

Add this project to a downstream `lakefile.toml` as a Git dependency:

```toml
[[require]]
name = "Hypertournaments"
git = "https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git"
rev = "FULL_CHECKED_COMMIT_SHA"
```

Replace the repository and revision with the intended public repository and
a commit whose complete CI passed. Keep the downstream Lean toolchain
compatible with that revision. The mathematical API remains under the
`Hypertournaments` namespace regardless of the GitHub repository name.

## Read the finite interfaces

Many class-level results use structures on `Fin m` so that a finite class
has one membership predicate for each cardinality. The main construction
lemmas also accept arbitrary finite vertex types. Reindexing is done by
actual embeddings or equivalences, and the mathematical structures retain
their intrinsic orientations.

For ordinary AP use `HasAP` for a local palette, or `FiniteClass.HasAP` for
an arbitrary finite class. For an omission family use
`HasStrongAmalgamation`; its last condition expresses exact overlap.
Chosen vertex orders appear only in the ordered expansion interfaces.

See [Verification](Verification) for the complete reproducibility checks
and [Mathematical definitions](Mathematical-definitions) for the conventions.
